newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria delays ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria delays ruling on Balkanbank insolvency.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Monday postponed ruling on an insolvency suit against state-owned Balkanbank by three months until experts complete a report on its financial condition, a court official said.

"The court delayed ruling until March 9. Until then three experts will have to prepare independent reports on the bank's assets-to-liabilities ratio at the moment when the central bank filed the suit," the official told reporters.

Balkanbank was put in receivership by the central bank on September 23 due to a capital-to-assets ratio of minus 37.85 percent and 5.471 billion levs of overdue payments. A bankruptcy procedure against it was launched on October 31.

State equity in Balkanbank rose to some 98 percent from around 76 percent after the bank's capital was boosted through a transfer of $60 million of dollar-denominated domestic bad loan bonds under a government decision in June.
The government issued the bonds in 1994 to cover non-performing loans extended by banks to state enterprises before 1991.

Local media reported recently that South Korea'a Daewoo Corp has shown an interest in buying a stake in the indebted bank as part of its plans for expansion on Bulgaria's banking and industrial market.
"Balkanbank has a negative net worth so its sale for one dollar could be agreed," a Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) official told Reuters. The BCC manages state equity in local commercial banks.

"We have had only preliminary talks with Daewoo on Balkanbank's sell-off, but we have not received a detailed offer so far," a central bank official said. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
